answer: Sustained attention queue requires each identity to keep a live beacon by answering a random micro-task within 90 seconds, with missed checks moving it to the back of the canyon of waiting work. An attacker must pay roughly 20 minutes of interrupted attention per identity daily, since each identity needs its own timed responses and cannot share one operator's focus. The system keeps a kernel of recent response timings and revokes voting weight when the queue shows batch-like patterns.
